claim: Domaine Dupasquier is a 15-hectare family vineyard in the hamlet of Aimavigne (Jongieux); booking is mandatory for vineyard walks/picnics, and a 3-hour visit-tasting-snack package is offered at €26 per person.
quote: Réservation obligatoire ... 26€ per person for a 3-hour experience with visit, refreshments, and tasting included.

claim: Domaine Dupasquier welcomes visitors Thursday-Saturday 10–12 and 14:30–18:30 year-round, and Tuesday-Saturday May 1 to Aug 26; David Dupasquier is the 5th generation winemaker working with sister Véronique and father Noël.
quote: The domaine welcomes visitors throughout the year on Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays from 10am–12pm and 2:30pm–6:30pm ... From May 1 to August 26, the estate is open from Tuesday to Saturday.

claim: Domaine Edmond Jacquin & Fils (106 Chemin de Vallières, 73170 Jongieux) is a 6th-generation family domaine open Monday-Saturday 9–12 and 14–18, with tastings of Jacquère, Altesse, Mondeuse, Gamay, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Crémant de Savoie.
quote: du lundi au samedi : 9h-12h et 14h-18h ... dégustations, visites du chai et rencontres conviviales autour des vins de Savoie

claim: Domaine Edmond Jacquin holds an annual portes-ouvertes (open cellar) event in April; the 2026 edition was held April 25–26 to discover Jongieux and Marestel appellations.
quote: Open house events were held April 25-26, 2026, offering an ideal opportunity to discover Savoie wines and the Jongieux and Marestel appellations.

claim: Domaine Chevallier Bernard in Jongieux runs an annual portes-ouvertes weekend (2 & 3 May 2026, 9:30–19:00) and produces Jacquère and Roussette whites alongside Gamay and Mondeuse reds.
quote: open cellar event on Saturday May 2nd and Sunday May 3rd from 9:30 am to 7:00 pm for wine tasting, sharing, relaxation and exchange.

claim: Domaine Carrel & Senger in Jongieux — winegrowers since 1830, six generations — is open Monday-Saturday 10–13 and 14–18, every day from 2 January to 31 December 2026.
quote: open from January 2 to December 31, 2026 from Monday to Saturday between 10 am and 1 pm and between 2 pm and 6 pm. A winegrower since 1830, their estate has endured for 6 generations in Jongieux.

claim: Château de la Mar in Jongieux, a restored castle on the Marestel terroir, opens for guided tours by reservation each summer from 22 July to 9 August.
quote: Château de la Mar is a beautifully restored castle producing exceptional wine on one of the most beautiful terroirs, Le Marestel. Tours of Château de la Mar are available from July 22 to August 9, upon reservation.

claim: The Marestel cru, AOC since 1973, climbs the western slopes of Mont du Chat above Jongieux on a steep pebbly terroir and is reserved for Roussette de Savoie made from the Altesse grape, yielding fresh, mineral whites with smoky, floral and almond notes.
quote: Marestel, named for a 16th Century landowner, climbs up the western slopes of the Mont du Chat mountain above the village of Jongieux ... wines, while fresh and minerally, often exhibit smoky, floral characters with hints of almond.

claim: The 3rd Festival du Cru Jongieux runs 18–19 July 2026 with a 2 km gourmet walk through the village, winemaker meetings, jazz and food pairings by two-Michelin-starred chef Mickaël Arnoult; tickets €80 until 30 June, €90 thereafter.
quote: third edition of the Festival du Cru Jongieux will be held on July 18-19, 2026 ... ticket price is set at €80 per person until June 30, 2026, and €90 until the day of the festival, including the gourmet walk and all wine and food pairings.

claim: The 'Loop around Jongieux' is a 10.6 km waymarked walk with 337 m elevation gain (about 4 hours, moderate), starting at Jongieux church and threading through hamlets, vineyards and forest with little traffic — suitable for families.
quote: The Loop around Jongieux is a 10.63 km walk with a vertical gain of 337 m, taking approximately 4 hours, with moderate difficulty ... starts near the church in Jongieux.

claim: The Route des Vins de Savoie comprises three signed itineraries; the northern route around Lac du Bourget links the Chautagne and Jongieux vineyards, with marked trails laced through the vines.
quote: Two routes criss-cross the Savoie department, with one north of Lac du Bourget taking in Chautagne and Jongieux.

claim: Domaine Renardat-Fâche in Mérignat (heart of Bugey) is an 8th-generation Cerdon producer, organic since 2008 and biodynamic-certified in 2022, specialising in the méthode ancestrale demi-sec sparkling rosé.
quote: Located in Mérignat, in the heart of Bugey, Estate Renardat-Fache embodies the excellence of Cerdon ... since 2008, the estate has embraced organic farming and obtained biodynamic certification in 2022.

claim: Bugey-Cerdon is a demi-sec pink sparkling made by méthode ancestrale — a single, incomplete spontaneous fermentation — and Patrick Bottex (hamlet of La Cueille) has produced it since the early 1980s and is credited with reviving the style.
quote: Patrick Bottex has been producing Bugey Cerdon in the tiny hamlet of La Cueille since the early 1980s, and is widely credited with helping to revive this traditional, alpine sparkling style.

claim: The Bugey cru Manicle is a tiny south-facing slope at the foot of a 500 m limestone cliff, worked by just four winegrowers, producing Pinot Noir reds and Chardonnay whites often compared to fine Burgundies.
quote: Manicle is an exceptional cru nestling at the foot of the cliffs, cultivated by 4 passionate winegrowers ... A few south-facing plots at the foot of a 500-meter limestone cliff that stores heat during the day and releases it at night.

claim: Le Caveau Bugiste runs a free tasting open to individuals and groups featuring Cuvée Amandier, Chardonnay Tradition and Manicle Blanc/Rouge — a one-stop tasting room for the Bugey range.
quote: The free tasting is open to individuals and groups, offering a perfect opportunity to sample the different wines on offer, such as the Cuvée Amandier, the Chardonnay Tradition, or the Manicle Blanc and Rouge.

claim: Mondeuse Noire is an ancient red variety indigenous to Savoie, cultivated by the Allobroges before the Roman conquest; classic wines are deep purple with sour-cherry, plum, pencil-lead and black-pepper notes and 10+ years ageing potential.
quote: Mondeuse is native to Savoie and has been cultivated by the Gallic tribe of Ancient Gaul (the Allobroges) prior to the Roman invasion ... notes of sour cherries, damson plums, pencil lead and a invigorating hint of black pepper.

claim: Jacquère (around 880 ha across Savoie) and Altesse (around 350 ha) are the workhorse white varieties of Savoie, expressing the alpine limestone-clay terroir with mineral, high-acid profiles.
quote: For the whites, Jacquère and Altesse account for 350 and 880 hectares respectively out of our 2,000 hectares under vine. The vineyards benefit from this unique limestone-clay terroir, which gives the wines their distinctive minerality and acidity.

claim: Private full-day Savoie wine tours depart from Chambéry or Aix-les-Bains with an English/French-speaking guide, visiting four historic vineyards across Chartreuse, Chaîne de l'Épine, Bauges and Combe de Savoie.
quote: private Savoie wine day tours from Chambéry or Aix-Les-Bains available through platforms like Klook, with English/French-speaking guides ... four historic vineyards in the regions of the Parc de Chartreuse, the Chaîne de l'Epine, the Parc des Bauges, and the Combe de Savoie.

claim: The Jongieux cru — the largest of the five Vin de Savoie crus — covers ~250 ha across multiple communes on steep south-west facing slopes of Mont du Chat, redesigned and terraced from 1990 by hand because the gradient defeats mechanisation.
quote: The Jongieux vineyard and neighboring communes cover 250 hectares with origins dating back to the 16th century, and was completely redesigned and consolidated starting in 1990 with significant terracing and soil restructuring work done manually.

claim: Compagnie des Bateaux operates cruises from Le Grand Port in Aix-les-Bains on 100% electric boats, including a Heritage cruise to Abbaye de Hautecombe, with adult fares starting from €18.
quote: Starting price: Adults from €18. Boats: 100% electric motorization. Heritage Cruise to Abbaye d'Hautecombe, featured as a recommended activity. Place Président Edouard Herriot, Le Grand Port, 73100 Aix-les-Bains.

claim: Compagnie des Bateaux du Lac du Bourget offers cruises from 1 hour to a full day with or without meals, including a 1-hour Discovery cruise, a half-day Canal de Savières cruise and a Heritage cruise with a Hautecombe Abbey stop, priced from €15 adult / €11 child.
quote: Options include a 1-hour Discovery cruise, a half-day cruise to navigate the Canal de Savières, and a Heritage cruise with a stop at Hautecombe Abbey. Prices start from 15€ for adults, 11€ for children.

claim: Abbaye d'Hautecombe is open Wednesday to Sunday from 10:00–11:15 and 14:30–17:00 for audioguided church visits; a Royal Apartments guided tour costs €7.50 (free under 12), and Mass is celebrated daily except Tuesday at noon.
quote: Du mercredi au dimanche de 10h à 11h15 et de 14h30 à 17h. Royal Apartments tour: €7.50 per person; free for children under 12. Messe à Hautecombe - Tous les jours sauf le mardi à 12h.

claim: Bateaucanal's Grand Tour from Chanaz is a 2h15 cruise covering the Canal de Savières, Lac du Bourget and canalized Rhône with lock passage; €18.50 adult / €11.50 child online from the village centre.
quote: Tarif spécial en ligne : 18,50 euros par adulte. Croisière d'une durée de 2h15. Les départs se font de Chanaz, dans le centre du village. Canal de Savières, Lac du Bourget et Rhône canalisé with passage d'une écluse.

claim: Bateaucanal operates daily cruises from 4 April to 25 October 2026 on three boats (Savoyard, Savoyard 2 and the new electro-solar Solely), with themed oenology, heritage and bee-keeping cruises and group offerings.
quote: du 4 Avril au 25 octobre 2026. The boats used are the Savoyard, Savoyard 2, and the new Solely electric-solar vessel. Themed event cruises (oenology, heritage, bee-keeping experiences, etc.).

claim: The lake's main beaches include Bourget-du-Lac (sand, aquatic games, volleyball), Les Mottets (sandy, BBQ areas), the Lido (small, accessed via the cycle path with a jumping dock), Aqualac (large sandy beach with pier), Mémard (shaded lawn) and quieter Conjux on the western shore.
quote: Plage du Bourget-du-Lac: Sanitaires, douches, parc arboré, plage de sable, jeux aquatiques. Plage du Lido: A smaller beach accessible via the cycling path… dock for jumping. Plage de Mémard: A grassy area with shade trees.

claim: Aix-les-Bains beaches are managed by Grand Lac with rigorous water-quality monitoring; Mémard near Le Grand Port is free with paddle and pedalo rentals, the Lido in Tresserve is free year-round but unsupervised, and Aqualac is the supervised municipal beach within a 3-hectare pool complex.
quote: All beaches benefit from oversight by Grand Lac, which conducts rigorous water quality monitoring. Plage de Mémard: free showers and accessible facilities. Centre Aqualac: une véritable plage municipale surveillée.

claim: YCBL at 221-223 Boulevard Ernest Coudurier in Le Bourget-du-Lac rents catamarans, windsurfs, kayaks, paddles, dinghies and Tiwal sailboats, with adult/teen/child courses and summer programmes from July 6 to August 28 2026.
quote: YCBL is a sailing club offering kayak, paddle, dinghy, catamaran and windsurfing rentals, along with courses for adults, teens and children. 221-223 Boulevard Ernest Coudurier 73370 LE BOURGET DU LAC. Summer stage registrations are open from Monday July 6 to Friday August 28, 2026.

claim: The tour of Lac du Bourget by bike is about 49 km with ~641 m of climbing and takes 2–3.5 hours; a voie verte runs between Les Mottets and Bourget-du-Lac, and the Col du Chat climb (6 km at 6%) can be bypassed via the cyclist tunnel or the Jongieux vineyard variant.
quote: 49 km with 641 m de dénivelé positif. Entre Chambéry et Aix-les-Bains, une voie verte permet de rouler en site propre. 6 km de montée à 6% de moyenne. Le tunnel du Chat (tunnel cycliste) allows bypassing this, or cyclists can take vineyard routes through Jongieux.

claim: The south shore is a protected natural area on a major European migration corridor hosting over 200 bird species and more than 20,000 wintering birds, with a mirador-style observation point; it also supports a reintroduction programme for the European pond turtle (Cistude d'Europe).
quote: le lac du Bourget est à la fois site d'hivernage d'intérêt mondial, de halte migratoire et de reproduction pour plus de 200 espèces d'oiseaux. Plus de 20 000 oiseaux y séjournent durant les mois d'automne et d'hiver. Un point d'observation de type mirador.

claim: Thermes Chevalley operate for the 2026 season from 2 February to 12 December for cures, with the spa welcoming the public from 24 January 2026 until 3 January 2027.
quote: The Thermes Chevalley will open for treatments from February 2 to December 12, 2026. The thermal spa will welcome the public from January 24, 2026 until January 3, 2027.

claim: Thermes Chevalley Aqua-détente is open daily 10:00–19:00; walk-in day access costs €25 weekdays and €27 on weekends, public holidays and school holidays.
quote: Access to the Aqua-détente space costs 25€ Monday to Friday and 27€ on weekends, public holidays, and school holidays. Spa Thermal - Espace Aqua-détente: Monday to Sunday from 10am to 7pm

claim: The Musée Faure is closed for renovation throughout 2026 and will reopen in early 2027 under a new identity, 'La Villa – Collection d'art'.
quote: The museum is temporarily closed. It will reopen in early 2027 under a new identity: La Villa-Collection d'art.

claim: The Musée Faure holds France's second-largest Rodin collection (34 sculptures) alongside Impressionist and post-Impressionist works by Cézanne, Degas, Pissarro and Sisley.
quote: le musée Faure contient 34 sculptures de Rodin, une collection de céramiques et faïences ainsi qu'une collection de souvenirs des séjours du poète Alphonse de Lamartine à Aix

claim: The Casino Grand Cercle, housed in the Palais de Savoie, is a listed historic monument inaugurated by Victor-Emmanuel II in 1850 and houses an 830-seat Italian-style theatre with a Salviati mosaic dome.
quote: inaugurated by King Victor-Emmanuel II of Savoy in 1850... a magnificent Italian-style theater seating 830, inaugurated in 1899 by architect Henri Eustache... the dome adorned with Salviati mosaics

claim: Aix-les-Bains tourist office runs a guided 'Belle Époque' walking circuit that strings together the Thermes, Casino Grand Cercle and former grand-hotel palaces.
quote: The Belle Époque circuit presents prestigious Aix-les-Bains as it was during the Belle Époque through a selection of heritage including the Thermes, Casino Grand Cercle, and former palaces.

claim: The Arch of Campanus is a 1st-century Roman funerary monument, 9.15 m high and 7.1 m wide, classified as a monument historique since 1890 and sited on a terrace overlooking the ancient thermae.
quote: The arch is 9.15 metres high and 7.1 metres wide, but only 75 centimetres deep, with limestone blocks placed without mortar and a single semicircular arch of 6 by 3.5 metres

claim: The Roman Temple of Diana is enclosed inside the Aix-les-Bains town hall on Place Maurice Mollard and can only be visited as part of a tourist-office guided 'Balade dans Aix' tour.
quote: Can only be visited as part of a guided tour, more information at the Tourist Office... situated within the Town Hall at Place Maurice Mollard

claim: Aix-les-Bains' marina, the largest freshwater pleasure port in France, comprises three sites — Petit Port (562 berths around the aquarium), Grand Port (933 boats) and Port de Mémard.
quote: The Petit Port of Aix-les-Bains, located around the aquarium, offers 562 places, a gas station and three different basins. Further south, the Grand Port welcomes 933 boats per year

claim: Compagnie des Bateaux d'Aix-les-Bains operates lake cruises (including a 1h15 'Découverte' loop) from the Grand Port reception pavilion.
quote: Boarding and disembarking takes place at the company's reception pavilion at the Grand Port of Aix-les-Bains.

claim: Aix-les-Bains' covered food market and producers' stalls run Wednesday and Saturday mornings; Wednesday is the bigger day, also adding clothing and textile stalls 09:00–18:00.
quote: There is a covered market and small producers market with gastronomy, food, and flowers on Wednesday and Saturday mornings. Fashion accessories, clothing, and textiles are available on Wednesday from 9am to 6pm.

claim: Thermes du Domaine de Marlioz sells day-spa packages (Aqua-Détente, Balnéo, Spa, Pour Soi) bundling pool/hammam/sauna access, aquagym, fitness room and lunch at restaurant La Dent du Chat.
quote: complete access to facilities (pool, hammam, sauna), participation in collective aquagym classes, access to the fitness room and lunch at the restaurant 'La Dent du Chat.'

claim: Le Bistrot du Port, at 2 Boulevard Robert Barrier facing the Grand Port, is a French bistro serving fully homemade dishes from fresh, local, seasonal produce with a lake-view terrace.
quote: The kitchen features entirely homemade cuisine prepared on-site from fresh, local, seasonal products.

claim: The Dent du Chat loop from Bourdeau is 14.7 km with 1,100 m elevation gain, ~7h20, rated Very Difficult, topping out at 1,458 m with panoramic Lac du Bourget views.
quote: Distance: 14.7 km / Elevation Gain: 1,100 m / Duration: 7 hours 20 minutes / Difficulty: Very difficult / Maximum Altitude: 1,458 m — magnificent panoramic view of the Lac du Bourget and the Alps.

claim: From La Chapelle-du-Mont-du-Chat the Dent du Chat + Roc de Cornillon route is shorter at ~6.8 km with +830 m, ~4h20, but still rated Difficult with cable/ladder sections unsuitable for those afraid of heights.
quote: The Dent du Chat and the Roc de Cornillon — Distance: 4.25 miles / Elevation gain: +2,720 ft / Duration: 4 hours 20 minutes / Difficulty: Difficult / Those who are afraid of heights may be affected by some technical sections equipped with cables or ladders.

claim: From the Relais du Mont du Chat car park, the Molard Noir out-and-back is only 2.76 km with 113 m gain in about 1 hour, rated Very Easy — the easiest way to bag a Mont du Chat ridge viewpoint.
quote: Distance: 2.76 km / Elevation Gain: 113 m / Duration: 1 hour / Difficulty: Très facile (Very Easy) — out-and-back hiking route that connects two scenic viewpoints: the Relais du Mont du Chat and Molard Noir.

claim: Molard Noir (1,452 m) is actually higher than Dent du Chat (1,390 m) and from its plateau opens a 360° panorama including Lac du Bourget, Aravis, Mont Blanc, Bauges, Vanoise, Belledonne and Chartreuse.
quote: From the small summit plateau, the view opens dramatically onto a 360° panorama including the Savoyard foothills, Lake Bourget, the Aravis, Mont Blanc, Bauges, Beaufortain, Vanoise, Lauzière, Belledonne, and Chartreuse when weather permits.

claim: La Chambotte belvedere at Saint-Germain-la-Chambotte is reached via stairs to a rooftop terrace, free, open year-round, with 360° views of the full Lac du Bourget and the Abbaye d'Hautecombe.
quote: 360° views over the Alps and surrounding area — visitors can see the Lac du Bourget, (the largest natural lake in France), in its entirety, as well as the Abbaye d'Hautecombe. Open all year round / Free of charge.

claim: La Chambotte sits at 725 m altitude, accessible by car with parking nearby, and is one of the postcard panoramas of the Lac du Bourget — Queen Victoria visited in 1887.
quote: At 725 m altitude, the Belvedere de la Chambotte offers you an exceptional 360° panorama of Lake Bourget — accessible by car, with a small parking nearby.

claim: The Grand Colombier (1,531 m, highest point of Bugey) has 11 marked trails of varying difficulty (2 very difficult, 3 hard, 5 medium), with ridge paths offering views of Mont Blanc, Lac du Bourget, the Rhône and Bugey.
quote: The Grand Colombier, the highest point of Bugey (1,531 m)... 11 marked hiking trails... Very difficult: 2, Hard: 3, Medium: 5, Quite difficult: 1 — The ridge trails promise a panoramic view of the Alps, Mont Blanc, Lake Bourget, the Rhone and Bugey.

claim: The full Grand Colombier loop from Culoz station is a serious sportive day: ~32.8 km with 1,600 m elevation gain over ~9 hours — long rather than technical.
quote: Distance: 32.8 km (round trip) / Elevation Gain: 1600m / Duration: 9 hours / Aucune difficulté hormis la longueur du parcours et les 1600m de dénivelé.

claim: From the Grand Colombier summit-parking lot, a 20-minute round-trip walk reaches the orientation table — the lazy option for the same panorama after driving up.
quote: From the parking lot at the top, it is possible to make a round trip of about twenty minutes to the orientation table, and several hikes of a few hours are also possible on the crests.

claim: Mont de la Charvaz (1,158 m) loop from Billième is ~8.4 km / +650 m / 4h, Medium difficulty, with a steep west-face ascent leading to twin viewpoints over the vineyard, Rhône canal, Bugey and Alps.
quote: Distance: Approximately 8.4 km / Elevation Gain: 650 meters / Duration: 4 hours / Difficulty: Medium — interesting vantage point over a portion of the Alps, the Bugey region, and the Avant-Pays Savoyard.

claim: Mont Tournier (877 m) loop is 10.95 km / +366 m / ~4h10 Moderate, with the Belvédère des Fils clifftop overlook of the canalised Rhône — no railings, not for kids/dogs.
quote: Distance: 10.95 km / Elevation Gain: +366 m / Duration: 4 hours 10 minutes / Difficulty: Moderate — Belvédère des Fils ... dramatic clifftop, though hikers should note the absence of safety railings.

claim: Mont Granier (1,933 m) from Entremont-le-Vieux is a serious 12 km / +1,100 m / 6h sporting hike with the technical Pas des Barres cabled section and the Balme à Colon cave tunnel — open May–November only.
quote: 1,100 meters of positive elevation gain, 12 kilometers, and 6 hours of hiking ... a technical section called Pas des Barres, where you must use cables and iron bars to pass through ... officially open from May 1 to November 30.

claim: Chanaz is officially labeled a Petite Cité de Caractère and nicknamed 'la petite Venise savoyarde', a stopover on the Canal de Savières with paved lanes and stone houses.
quote: Chanaz se dévoile comme une charmante escale au bord du canal de Savières. […] les ruelles pavées et les maisons en pierres créent une atmosphère intimiste

claim: Daily boat cruises from Chanaz on the Canal de Savières, Lac du Bourget and canalised Rhône (with lock passage) operate from 4 April to 25 October 2026.
quote: Daily trips on the Canal de Savières, Lake Bourget and the canalized Rhone with lock passage are offered from April 4 to October 25, 2026.

claim: The Moulin de Chanaz, a Historic-Monument-classified artisanal oil mill in operation since 1868, presses walnuts and hazelnuts with stone millstones and offers visits with tastings.
quote: The Moulin de Chanaz is located in Savoie on the heights of Chanaz and has been transforming nuts and hazelnuts according to traditional craftsmanship since 1868.

claim: Yenne's weekly market is held every Thursday morning from 7:30 to 12:30 on the central square (Place Charles Dullin).
quote: tous les jeudi matin de 7h30 à 12h30 […] sur la place centrale de la ville

claim: Yenne's Église Notre-Dame-de-l'Assomption, built 12th–15th c., has been a classified Historic Monument since 1987 and features historiated capitals, Gothic stalls and rose windows.
quote: The Church of Notre-Dame de l'Assomption, founded on the basis of Romanesque style, has been listed as a Historic Monument since April 6, 1987.

claim: Belley's weekly market runs every Saturday morning 7:30–12:30 along Grande Rue, Place des Terreaux and Boulevard de Verdun, with around 90 stallholders.
quote: tous les samedis matins de 7 h 30 à 12 h 30 […] Grande rue, place des Terreaux et boulevard de Verdun […] Environ 90 forains sont présents

claim: Jean-Anthelme Brillat-Savarin was born in Belley in 1755 in the family house at 62 Grande Rue, and his quips ('Tell me what you eat, I'll tell you who you are') anchor the town's gastronomic identity.
quote: Jean Anthelme BRILLAT-SAVARIN was born in Belley on April 2nd 1755 in the family house located today at No. 62 Grande Rue.

claim: Belley's neo-Gothic Cathédrale Saint-Jean-Baptiste was largely rebuilt in the 19th century, retains the 12th-c. north portal and a 15th-c. chancel, with a 40-m bell tower.
quote: The neo-gothic Cathedral of St. John the Baptist was largely rebuilt in the 19th century while retaining the northern door from the original 12th-century cathedral

claim: Le Bourget-du-Lac's Prieuré was built c. 1030 for Cluny monks; its cloister has a 13th-c. Romanesque upper gallery and 15th-c. Gothic lower gallery, plus a French formal garden.
quote: Construit autour de 1030 pour les moines de Cluny, le Prieuré possède un cloître aux magnifiques voûtes

claim: The Pierre qui Vire at Saint-Genix-les-Villages is a legendary monolith on the GR9 that, per local lore, makes a tiny turn on itself on Christmas Eve, with a panoramic view over the Rhône valley.
quote: According to legend, this is one of those stones about which it is said that on Christmas Eve it makes a small turn on itself.

claim: The Jongieux cru spans the communes of Billième, Jongieux, Lucey, Saint-Jean-de-Chevelu and Yenne (250–500 m altitude) — the largest Vin de Savoie cru, well suited to cellar-door visits.
quote: extends across the communes of Billième, Jongieux, Lucey, Saint-Jean-de-Chevelu, and Yenne, ranging from 250 to 500 meters in altitude

claim: The Château du Châtelard at Yenne is a 14th-c. former maison forte that was the seat of the Châtelard seigneury, one of several fortified houses around Yenne.
quote: Château du Châtelard est un ancien 14th-century stronghouse, which in the Middle Ages was the seat of the Châtelard seigneury on the commune of Yenne

claim: The Maison Forte des Rubods at Saint-Paul-sur-Yenne can be visited on a 2-hour guided tour led by a Savoie Mont Blanc Patrimoine Guide together with the owner.
quote: a unique 2-hour immersion into the history of this property. The program includes a guided tour, exchange with the owner and the Patrimoine Guide.

claim: Chanaz also houses a Gallo-Roman museum presenting the Portout potters, plus craftsmen (jeweller, microbrewery, roaster) alongside the period mill and restaurants for all budgets.
quote: The Gallo-Roman museum welcomes you and introduces you to the history of potters from Portout

claim: Château des Ducs de Savoie museum is free entry, open Tue-Fri 14h-18h and 10h-13h/14h-18h on weekends/holidays/summer school breaks; guided tour of Sainte-Chapelle runs 04/05-23/06/2026 Tue-Thu from 14h30 with booking required, 5.50-7.50€.
quote: Entrée gratuite. Ouvert le mardi, mercredi, jeudi et vendredi de 14h à 18h. Les jours fériés, week-ends et vacances scolaires d'été de 10h à 13h et de 14h à 18h.

claim: The Fontaine des Éléphants was built in 1838 in tribute to General de Boigne, a Chambéry benefactor; it stands 17.65 m tall with four cast-iron elephants arranged as a cross of Savoy.
quote: This fountain was built in 1838 to pay tribute to General de Boigne, a major benefactor of Chambéry, his native town. The fountain shows in its plane a cross of Savoy, represented by four elephants united by their rump.

claim: The Musée Savoisien reopened after an 8-year closure and major renovation, housed in a 13th-century former Franciscan convent, with a refreshed scenography of films, interactive displays and handle-able objects; admission is free.
quote: the Musée Savoisien, the departmental museum of the history and cultures of Savoie, reopened its doors to the public after eight years of closure for major works

claim: Chambéry to Jongieux is roughly 25 km by road and about 27 minutes' drive, primarily via Route du Tunnel and the D210, putting Chambéry within the 30 km radius from Jongieux.
quote: The driving distance from Chambéry to Jongieux is 25.2 kilometers and takes approximately 27 minutes. The route is primarily via Route du Tunnel and D 210.

claim: The Musée des Beaux-Arts opens daily except Mondays and public holidays 10h-18h (extended to 20h on the first Thursday of each month), with permanent collection access free; its strength is 14th-18th c. Italian schools (Sienese Bartolo di Fredi, Florentine Santi di Tito, Neapolitan Baroque Luca Giordano).
quote: Italian works from the 14th to 18th centuries are particularly well represented, with a chronological tour... Sienese school (Bartolo di Fredi), the Florentine school (Santi di Tito), and Neapolitan Baroque (Luca Giordano)

claim: Les Charmettes, Rousseau's house museum at 890 chemin des Charmettes, opens Tue-Sun 10h-18h from 1 April to 31 October and weekends only in winter; gardens are free year-round.
quote: From April 1st to October 31st: Open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm. Closed on Mondays and public holidays. From November 1st to March 31st: Open on weekends from 10am to 6pm.

claim: The covered Halles de Chambéry market runs Tuesday-Saturday 6h-13h30; Place de Genève hosts an open-air food market Saturday morning and Tuesday 7h-12h, plus a Wed-evening market (April-October 16h-20h) limited to organic/short-supply-chain producers within 30 km of Chambéry.
quote: Tuesday Market: Place de Genève, every Tuesday from 7h to 12h... Wednesday Evening Market: From April 1st to the end of October 2026, the market runs from 16h to 20h... organic agriculture and short supply chains (30 km maximum around Chambéry). Saturday Market: Food producers occupy Place de Genève on Saturday.

claim: Chambéry old town is a network of paved streets, covered passages and arcades; Rue de Boigne (the 'porticos') links the château to the Fontaine des Éléphants, while Place Saint-Léger is the main pedestrian artery and natural starting point for a walking tour.
quote: Rue de Boigne, which connects the castle to the Fountain of Elephants, is renowned for its arcades and shops. These arcades are nicknamed 'the porticos' by locals.
